diagnostic_evidence.quote: The holes \(D_j \subset \mathbb C \), for \(j \in [M]\) are open, simply-connected sets and have disjoint closure.
Note that $|D|/b<1$ as the total area of the holes, $|D| = \sum_{j\in[M]} |D_j|$, is always less than the area of the torus, $|\mathbb{T}_\tau| = b$.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption 1 imposes only planar conditions on the holes and never requires them to be embedded in the torus (e.g., contained in a fundamental parallelogram). For configurations it permits, the construction Ω = T_τ \ D̄ need not be a connected finitely-connected torus with M boundary components and the results fail: (i) a single hole D_1 = B(c, 0.75) on the unit square torus satisfies Assumption 1, covers the whole torus (Ω = ∅), and falsifies Lemma 3.2, since at a torus point with two lattice translates inside D_1 the Green computation gives 2 − |D_1|/b rather than the claimed 1 − |D_1|/b; (ii) a simply connected band-shaped hole wrapping around the torus makes P_τ \ D̄ disconnected, breaking the connectedness step in the proof of Lemma 3.3(4) (the claimed dim N(D − ½I) = M−1 is then wrong); (iii) the assertion '|D|/b < 1 ... always' used in the proof of Lemma 3.3(6) is implied by no hypothesis (nothing prevents Σ|D_j| ≥ b).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to Assumption 1 the standard condition that each D_j lies in a fundamental parallelogram (equivalently, projects injectively onto T_τ with pairwise disjoint closed images); this yields |D| < b and the connectedness/topology the proofs use, and all arguments then apply unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: For geometries allowed by the stated hypotheses, the domain construction is ill-defined or degenerate and Gauss' lemma, the nullspace characterization, the Fredholm arguments, and all three main theorems are unreliable as stated.
issues.title: Assumption 1 does not ensure the holes are embedded in the torus; permitted geometries falsify the stated results
issues.why_classification: A standard one-line local hypothesis addition restores every claim, method, and advertised scope; no proof architecture changes and only unintended degenerate configurations are excluded.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where \(z_0^{+}\) and \(z_0^{-}\) denote the limits as \(z \to z_0\) from \(\Omega\) and \(D\), respectively.
Suppose that the fixed \(\gamma > 0\) is small enough so that we can express $z = z_0-h\nu(z_0) \in\partial\Omega$, for $h = \vert z- z_0 \vert$.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 3.3(2) asserts one-sided limits of D[φ] as z → z_0 from Ω with arbitrary approach, which is what the Dirichlet boundary condition requires. In the proof, the local singular estimate (II) is obtained only for z on the normal line z = z_0 − hν(z_0): the key inequality |z−ξ|² ≥ ½(|z−z_0|² + |z_0−ξ|²) used for (II) is derived under exactly this restriction, and the stated reduction — 'We only need to consider for such z since D[φ] is continuous on Ω' — is a non sequitur: continuity of the potential inside Ω does not convert arbitrary boundary limits into normal ones. The claimed general limits are therefore not established by the proof.

failure_location.quote: We only need to consider for such $z$ since $\mathcal{D}[\phi]$ is continuous on $\Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supplement the proof with the standard missing argument: uniformity in z_0 of the normal-limit estimates together with a nearest-point-projection argument, or invoke the general-approach proofs in the cited references (Kress Thm. 6.18, Folland Thm. 3.22).
issues.overall_effect: The boundary traces of the double-layer potential, used to verify the Dirichlet boundary condition in Theorem 3.1 and in the proof of Lemma 3.5(2) ('by Lemma 3.3(1)–(2)'), are proven only for normal approach as written.
issues.title: Jump relation for the double-layer potential is proven only for normal approach to the boundary
issues.why_classification: The missing step is standard and contained; the statements are true and no downstream claim, rate, or scope changes once it is supplied.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The result directly follows from the Sokhotski-Plemelj formula \cite[Thm. 7.8]{kress1989linear}.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation (3.11) defines f_D with the arc-length measure |dξ| in the ζ-integral, but the paper's own derivation (which uses dξ = iν|dξ| for the boundary orientation) shows the complex line element dξ is required; the proof silently switches from dξ to |dξ| between its two displays. For the object as defined, Re f_D[φ] ≠ D[φ]: for a single circular hole with constant density φ ≡ 1 and z the disk center, the ζ-term vanishes (ζ is odd and η_1(z−ξ) is linear, so both integrals over the circle vanish) and the second term evaluates to −|D|/b, so Re f_D[1](center) = −|D|/b, whereas D[1](center) = 1 − |D|/b by Lemma 3.2. The jump relation (2) likewise fails (the jump of the arc-length Cauchy-type integral is −iν̄(z_0)φ(z_0), not ∓φ(z_0)/2), and its proof misapplies the Sokhotski–Plemelj formula, which concerns the complex line element dξ, not arc length.

failure_location.quote: In fact, $\Re  f_\mathcal{D}[\phi] = \mathcal{D}[\phi]$, which is a function on $\mathbb T_\tau\backslash\partial\Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace |dξ| by dξ in the first integral of (3.11) and in the matching display of the proof; Re f_D = D[φ] then follows from the paper's own intermediate derivation, the jump relation follows from the standard Plemelj formula applied to the resulting Cauchy integral, and the downstream proofs go through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Claims (1)–(2) of Lemma [Complex layer] are false for the defined object; the complex-potential arguments in the proofs of Lemma 3.3(4) (nullspace of D − ½I), Lemma 3.5(2) (injectivity of D + X − ½I), and Theorem 3.1 (the Dirichlet BVP), which invoke this lemma, are unsound as written.
issues.title: Complex double-layer potential is defined with the arc-length measure where the complex line element is required, making Lemma [Complex layer] false as stated
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained and loses no mathematical content, but it requires correcting a definition, replacing an invalid proof step (the Plemelj application) with a correct argument, and re-verifying a central lemma on which the main Dirichlet theorem's proof rests — more than a routine local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, we can uniquely choose $\phi_k$ satisfying $\mathcal{M}\phi = -\mathcal{M}\mathcal{S}[\psi_k](z_0)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The right-hand side of Theorem 3.3's eigenproblem is σ_k S_0[φ_k] = σ_k(S[φ_k − φ̄_k] + φ̄_k), but the stated discrete problem uses σ S(I−M)φ⃗, omitting the discretization of the mean term φ̄ (i.e., +Mφ⃗). Its continuous analogue (D*+½)(I−M)φ = σS[(I−M)φ] is not equivalent to (3.8): taking means forces its solutions to satisfy M[S[(I−M)φ]] = 0, whereas eigenfunctions of (3.8) satisfy φ̄ = −M S[ψ_k], which is generally nonzero because Steklov eigenfunctions are single-layer potentials only up to an additive constant (Theorem 3.2's '+C'; the obstruction vanishes only if S[1]|_{∂Ω} is constant, which fails generically). Hence the stated discrete problem solves a different eigenproblem and can miss Steklov eigenvalues (reduced multiplicity or absent); it is also a degenerate pencil, since constant vectors lie in the kernel of both sides for every σ, so it does not deliver the eigenpairs of Theorem 3.3 as claimed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the displayed eigenproblem to discretize S_0, e.g. (D_s + ½)(I−M)φ⃗ = σ[S(I−M)+M]φ⃗ (equivalently σ(I−M)S(I−M)φ⃗), which also removes the degenerate constant direction, and recover φ̄ from the eigenvector as prescribed in the proof of Theorem 3.3.
issues.overall_effect: The Steklov solver described in Appendix C.3, if implemented as stated, computes wrong/missing eigenvalues and leaves the eigenfunction constant undetermined, so the Steklov computations of Examples 4–6 are not reproducible from the described algorithm (the reported agreement with reference values indicates the actual implementation differed from the stated formula).
issues.title: Discrete Steklov eigenproblem omits the mean term of the modified single-layer potential and is not a discretization of the stated BIE
issues.why_classification: The stated algorithm's guarantee (computing the Steklov spectrum of Theorem 3.3) fails, and the repair requires recognizing the inequivalence (the constant-shift obstruction) and constructing the correct discrete operator — a contained correction with no mathematical loss, but more than a routine symbol fix.
